segments.caption: Adelaide, 2014. The final day. India need 122, with eight wickets in hand.
Their captain is 26, in his first Test in charge.
Rewind four days.
It's a Test played in grief, two weeks after Phillip Hughes's death.
Australia bat first and pile up 517. Warner, Clarke and Smith all make hundreds.
MS Dhoni is injured, so Virat Kohli leads India.
The first ball he faces from Mitchell Johnson hits him on the helmet. He gets up, and makes 115.
Warner makes another hundred. Australia declare. India need 364 on the final day.
Most captains would settle for a draw. Kohli's India go for the win.
Day five. Dhawan falls for 9. Pujara for 21. 57 for 2.
Kohli walks out. 307 still to get.
He doesn't block. He goes after Nathan Lyon, Australia's best weapon on a turning pitch.
Against Lyon, Kohli scores 74, off 82 balls.
With Murali Vijay holding the other end, India reach tea on 205 for 2. 159 to win, in one session.
Kohli reaches his hundred, off 135 balls. His second of the match, in his first Test as captain. Only Greg Chappell had ever done that.
242 for 2. 122 to win. The impossible chase is on.
Then Lyon finds a way.
Vijay, lbw for 99. In the same over, Rahane is given out caught, off his pad. There's no DRS in this series.
Rohit goes. Saha swings, and is bowled. As wickets fall around him, Kohli keeps swinging. 41 runs, off 40 balls.
He's on 141. India need 60. He pulls Lyon, and Mitchell Marsh takes the catch on the boundary.
India lose eight wickets for 73. Australia win by 48. Lyon takes 12 in the match.
But Kohli's 256 runs are the most by an Indian in his first Test as captain. Within a month, the captaincy is his.
India lost a Test that day. They found a captain.
Beyond The Scoreboard.
